title: Analytical Electron Microscopy with Cathodoluminescence to Classify Structural Defects Impeding Charge Transport in Power Electronics
content: Monoclinic (β-phase) Ga2O3 has become an emerging semiconductor due to its high-breakdown electric field for future power electronics [1]. While multiple recent synthesis advances promise the supply of large-size, high-purity wafers, structural defects still prevail in epitaxial films grown on substrates and potentially serve as charge-carrier traps that limit diode performance [2]. Minimizing performance-killing defects through crystallographic structure control during epitaxial growth is an effective strategy for commercializing β-Ga2O3 in power device applications. However, it requires the prerequisite knowledge about individual defect structure and its properties. The optoelectronic property of structural defects in β-Ga2O3 and their development into micrometer-sized surface features have not been fully explored. Here, we use a multimodal microscopy approach to measure the structure and property of two surface features: (1) carrot- and (2) line-shapes, prevalent on epitaxial film surface grown on the <010> substrate and characterize the constituent planar defects to elucidate the underlying detrimental effect on device performance.
